problem: Pipeline completes but rul_rmse=0.206(target 0.08) MISS, mono_violation=0.474(target 0.01) MISS; fault_f1=0.997 PASS
action: Generated 5 result plots; found Hybrid(17ep) and PINN(57ep) hit IDENTICAL RUL floor (rmse 0.206,R2 0.09) => label-limited; PINN Paris C/m frozen at init (l_paris~1e-8, no gradient)

problem: RUL floor confirmed: dataset is steady-state seeded-fault (12 conditions), NOT run-to-failure. rul_relative is synthetic FPT-piecewise ramp to class floor; 58% of windows pinned at 1.0; per-window signal stationary within a recording so label depends on window POSITION not content
action: Inspected labels_fpt.parquet + rul_labels_v2.py; benchmarked piecewise-FPT labeling, PINN Paris, GradNorm multi-task balancing
impact: True continuous RUL not learnable from this data; classification (99.7%) is real. Decision pending on data/reframe strategy

problem: Needed a from-scratch design for wind-turbine pitch-bearing RUL: continuous RUL alone is a weak signal and physics-free NNs don't extrapolate past their training distribution
action: Built dual-track system: Hybrid track (TCN-Transformer + Channel-Temporal Mixed-MLP + cross-attention, ~30M params) for pattern-rich fault/RUL regression; PINN track (TCN backbone + Paris-law residual loss with learnable crack-growth constants C,m, ~10M params) to constrain RUL to be physically monotonic and derive an absolute time-to-failure from crack length instead of only a relative 0-1 score; both distilled into a ~5M-param student exported as INT8 (edge) and FP16+MC-dropout (cloud). FPT-piecewise RUL labels + run-level (file_idx) splits chosen over naive window splits to avoid leakage across the same physical run. Full rationale already in README.md ('Why this project', 'Architecture', 'Paris-law derivation chain' sections) -- not duplicated here.
impact: Established the baseline dual-track pipeline (00-07 stages); later found (entry 7) the underlying dataset is steady-state, not run-to-failure, which limits how much the Paris-law term can actually contribute

problem: Training under-utilized the H100: batch 64 not TensorCore-aligned, only 4 dataloader workers, cuDNN SDP/TF32 not enabled, manual Python .item() spike-guards blocking CUDA graph capture
action: Batch 64->256 (TensorCore-aligned) with lr 2e-4/1e-4 sqrt-scaled; workers 4->8, prefetch_factor 2->4, drop_last=True (uniform batch shapes needed for CUDA graph capture); apply_cudnn_settings enables Flash SDP + TF32 matmul; torch.compile mode set to max-autotune; added optional ptwt (vectorized wavelet) path in feature_extractor, ~4x faster than pywt on CPU. Decided against manual CUDA graphs because .item() spike-guard calls are hard CPU-GPU syncs that break graph capture -- left compile's max-autotune to handle static subgraphs instead.
impact: Full H100 utilization pass; established the sqrt LR-scaling convention reused in every later batch-size change

problem: Moved to H200 (141GB HBM3e vs H100 80GB) with identical GH100 die/TFLOPs -- compute unchanged but VRAM headroom unused at batch 256
action: Batch 256->1024 (4x, VRAM-bound scaling since compute is unchanged); LR scaled by sqrt(1024/256)=2x per the sqrt-scaling rule adopted in entry 9 (gradient noise scales as 1/sqrt(batch), so LR should scale as sqrt(batch) to hold the effective step size roughly constant)
impact: 4x fewer optimizer steps per epoch at the same compute; later superseded by the batch-8192 change in entry 15

problem: 60-90 min wasted per run: (1) shared_test_path=None hardcoded in make_loaders so the test set re-extracted features from scratch every run instead of loading the pre-built test_windows.npz; (2) no disk cache for train/val splits, so 375k+78k windows were re-processed from raw parquet on every single run
action: Passed args.shared_test / resolved npz path through instead of None; added feat_cache_dir to PitchBearingDataset saving train_{hash}.npz + val_{hash}.npz on first run, auto-invalidated via an md5 key over parquet path/split ratios/filter/window geometry so a stale cache can't silently be reused after a config change. PINN track reuses the same dataset_cache/ dir the hybrid track writes so the second track loads instantly.
impact: First run still pays the one-time extraction cost; every subsequent run loads in ~2 min instead of 60-90 min

problem: No automated coverage of the 00-07 pipeline; regressions (like entries 1-5) were only caught by full HPC runs costing hours per iteration
action: Added a pytest suite (tests/conftest.py, tests/test_pipeline.py, tests/constants.py) exercising the pipeline end-to-end at small scale; hardened scripts/00-07 with stricter checks; small fixes to compare_v2.py and track_hybrid/model.py surfaced by the new tests
impact: Regressions catchable locally in minutes instead of during multi-hour HPC runs

problem: scripts/02_build_dataset.sh and hpc_train.sbatch needed hardening for unattended SLURM runs (resume-safety, path resolution) after the feature-cache change in entry 11 introduced new cache-dir state to manage
action: Extended dataset_v2.py cache handling; reworked 02_build_dataset.sh and hpc_train.sbatch to correctly create/detect the feature cache dir across job resubmissions
impact: SLURM resubmission after preemption no longer redoes feature extraction

problem: Long unattended stages (parquet scan, epoch loops, distillation) gave no live feedback, making it hard to tell a hang apart from a slow-but-working run in HPC logs
action: Added tqdm progress bars to parquet row-group scanning (dataset_v2.py) and the train/distill epoch + batch loops
impact: HPC log tailing now shows live throughput/ETA instead of silence between stage prints

problem: Profiling found remaining CPU-bound and sync-bound waste: parquet row-groups read serially, window extraction used per-window Python loops, PINNLoss looped per unique run_id in Python, GradScaler added an unscale+inf-check sync every step, running-loss used float(.item()) every step (6 host-device syncs/step); distill.py never called apply_cudnn_settings at all (separate from the entry-1 SDP guard, which only disables SDP but doesn't enable TF32/Flash/benchmark)
action: Parallelized parquet row-group reads with ProcessPoolExecutor (top-level _read_parquet_rg worker, falls back to serial for small files); replaced per-window Python loops with np.lib.stride_tricks.sliding_window_view in window/normalization extraction; vectorized PINNLoss Paris/monotonicity terms by sorting the batch by (run_id, win_idx) and masking same-run consecutive pairs instead of looping torch.unique(run_id); dropped GradScaler entirely in hybrid/pinn/distill (bf16 autocast has the full fp32 exponent range so loss scaling is unnecessary); accumulate running loss as an on-GPU detached tensor and call .item() only once at epoch end; batch 4096->8192 with LR rescaled by sqrt(2) per the entry-9/10 convention; torch.compile mode switched max-autotune->reduce-overhead, chosen because max-autotune's longer autotune search stalled resumed runs while reduce-overhead gives faster/more stable per-step time under recompiles; distill.py now calls apply_cudnn_settings() and also compiles the frozen teachers (reduce-overhead) since they are inference-only and never exported -- the student stays uncompiled because export_edge_int8/export_cloud_fp16 need type(student)()+jit.trace, which a torch.compile wrapper breaks; run_all.sh gained a --fresh flag to wipe all sentinels/checkpoints/cache for a from-scratch rerun; added PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True to reduce allocator fragmentation at the larger batch size
impact: Not yet committed to git; batch-8192 change and the compile-mode switch have not yet been benchmarked end-to-end on HPC. The compare_v2.py/inference.py changes sitting in this same working-tree diff duplicate entries 3/5 (already journaled, just still uncommitted)

problem: Needed to pick one laptop (hard budget cap set by the user) that can run three unrelated workloads to completion: this repo's RUL training, an OpenFOAM CFD case, and a distributed eigenvalue/stability solver -- weighted equally
action: Wrote scripts/estimate_hw_time.py: a resource model anchored to two MEASURED datapoints (this repo's H200 windows/s throughput for DL, and a measured 7.5h/20-core CFD run) rather than pure FLOP-counting, because these small 0.3-3.7M-param nets never saturate a big GPU and a naive FLOP model under-predicts wall-time; documented findings in docs/laptop_selection_analysis.md concluding RUL training is ~95%+ parallel and CUDA-only (this repo's code path is GPU-locked -- enable_cudnn_sdp(False), Flash-SDP, torch.compile CUDA graphs all assume NVIDIA), while the CFD/eigensolver workloads are CPU-only (MPI, no GPU path)
impact: Advisory only, no repo code changed; laptop choice keyed off whether the machine has a CUDA GPU since only the RUL workload benefits from one

problem: v3 physics-anchored RUL track (approved plan): NN must predict damage state, not time. Needed ordinal severity axis + run-level physical damage evidence
action: Added v3/severity_axis.py (9 ordinal levels from A_MAP_M anchors, interval-censored log-a targets), v3/signal_physics.py (CuPy/NumPy envelope spectrum SNR at BPFO/BPFI/BSF/FTF harmonics, dual-impulse lag -> spall length, PHYS_DIM=37), v3/build_physfeat.py stage-10 driver (GPU/CPU-pool/mpi4py backends, JSONL resume checkpointing), scripts/10_v3_physfeat.sh. Key finding: at 1-3 rpm fault freqs are sub-Hz so physics features MUST be run-level (window cannot resolve them) -- also positionally safe
impact: Stage 10 smoke-tested on synthetic parquet (12 runs); dual-impulse recovers 0.399s vs 0.4s truth; severity axis self-test passes

problem: v3 needed the damage-state model: fault class + ordinal severity + heteroscedastic crack length, trained WITHOUT any time-like target
action: Added v3/losses.py (CORN conditional ordinal loss, interval-censored Gaussian NLL via ndtr), v3/damage_net.py (TCNBlock reuse from track_pinn, 3 heads, 0.34M params), v3/dataset_v3.py (wraps PitchBearingDataset, attaches run-level phys features z-scored on train-run stats + severity targets; group-mean fallback for stale tables), v3/train.py (bf16, compile, guards from v2 convention, checkpoint_last.pt EVERY epoch with RNG state for crash-safe resume, V3_RESULTS_DIR env override), scripts/11_v3_train.sh
impact: Smoke: 2-epoch train on synthetic parquet passes (loss 5.60->4.85), resume-from-checkpoint verified (cache hit + epoch 3 continuation)

problem: Needed damage->RUL conversion with uncertainty and a calibration stage
action: Added v3/paris_engine.py: closed-form Paris cycles (matches v2 loop integrator <0.03%), MC over (a0 from NN posterior, C lognormal 0.35, class->Kt from posterior), inverse-Gaussian moment fit + closed-form quantile for deployment, NumPy/CuPy/mpi4py backends; v3/calibrate.py stage 12 split-conformal sigma scaling on val; scripts/12. PHYSICS FINDING: TTF is NOT monotone in crack length across classes -- IRC (sharp crack Kt=2.4, 0.5mm) has ~700h vs IRS (blunt spall Kt=1.8, 1.5mm) ~727h; only terminal ordering (IORW ~6h << all) is guaranteed. Must be surfaced in expert report
impact: MC RUL p5/p50/p95 + IG fit agree (720 vs 724h); calibration smoke passes (coverage 67%->95% on synthetic)

problem: Failure-mode propagation intimation: both severity escalation and physics graph (user choice)
action: Added v3/propagation.py: reuses the tribology PROGRESSION_GRAPH DAG (common/rul_labels.py), edge sojourn = closed-form Paris time between class anchors under destination Kt, current-window a-hat refines outgoing edges, risk = posterior-weighted rate-normalised over successors, Dijkstra shortest-time path to terminal IORW, ETA CIs from combined C-scatter + damage-sigma lognormal; stage-13 CLI writes propagation_table.json for expert review; scripts/13
impact: Self-test passes; sojourn table physically coherent (IORS->IORW 13.5h ... Health->ORC 2629h); 18 edges materialised

problem: Lightweight portable deployable model (user requirement): ONNX Runtime, no torch at inference
action: Added v3/export_onnx.py (opset-17 tuple-output export, fp32 parity check vs torch, onnxruntime dynamic INT8, model_meta.json carries phys_norm+sigma_scale), v3/inference_v3.py (torch-free V3Predictor: scipy bandpass -> windows -> 160-D features with common.config stub when torch absent -> phys features -> ONNX -> window aggregation -> MC RUL -> propagation; zeros-fallback if feature extractor missing), scripts/14. Fixed float32 prob normalisation in mc_rul and filtered already-passed anchor states from propagation rates. FINDING: INT8 (0.40MB) is SLOWER than fp32 (1.37MB, 2.2ms/window) on x86 for this tiny conv net -> fp32 is the default deploy artifact, INT8 kept for size-constrained edge
impact: fp32 parity 6e-7; full prediction dict (RUL p5/p50/p95, HI, crack mm CI, 12-class probs, severity stage, propagation w/ ETAs) JSON-serializable in both fp32 and int8 modes
